title: Checks for an iterator or string search (such as find(), position(), or rposition()) followed by a call to is_some() or is_none().
summary: Readability, this can be written more concisely as: Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks if the seek method of the Seek trait is called with SeekFrom::Current(0), and if it is, suggests using stream_position instead.
summary: Readability. Use dedicated method. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for jumps to the start of a stream that implements Seek and uses the seek method providing Start as parameter.
summary: Readability. There is a specific method that was implemented for this exact scenario. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for explicit self-assignments.
summary: Self-assignments are redundant and unlikely to be intentional. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Warns when constructors have the same name as their types.
summary: Repeating the name of the type is redundant. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks that module layout uses only mod.rs files.
summary: Having multiple module layout styles in a project can be confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for self receiver that is only used in recursion with no side-effects.
summary: It may be possible to remove the self argument, allowing the function to be used without an object of type Self. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Looks for blocks of expressions and fires if the last expression returns () but is not followed by a semicolon.
summary: The semicolon might be optional but when extending the block with new code, it doesn’t require a change in previous last line. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests moving the semicolon after a block to the inside of the block, after its last expression.
summary: For consistency it’s best to have the semicolon inside/outside the block. Either way is fine and this lint suggests inside the block. Take a look at semicolon_outside_block for the other alternative. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests moving the semicolon from a block’s final expression outside of the block.
summary: For consistency it’s best to have the semicolon inside/outside the block. Either way is fine and this lint suggests outside the block. Take a look at semicolon_inside_block for the other alternative. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Warns if literal suffixes are separated by an underscore.
summary: To enforce separated literal suffix style, see the unseparated_literal_suffix lint. Suffix style should be consistent. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for misuses of the serde API.
summary: Serde is very finicky about how its API should be used, but the type system can’t be used to enforce it (yet?). Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for usage of contains to see if a value is not present in a set like HashSet or BTreeSet, followed by an insert.
summary: Using just insert and checking the returned bool is more efficient. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.
